clue.text: Political adventurer hijacking fabulous air transport?

parts.note: the flying carpet of fable, as in the Arabian Nights, is a fabulous means of air travel
someone hijacking a thing is bagging it, grabbing it for themselves, so is a bagger

explanation.surface: A political opportunist seizes control of some legendary aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads the answer as 'one who bags (hijacks) a magic carpet'. A carpetbagger was originally a Northern opportunist in the post-Civil War American South, carrying belongings in a carpet bag.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names an outsider who moves into a district to exploit it politically, an opportunist adventurer.

clue.text: Topping features of, sporting trophy also perhaps

parts.note: a cup is the classic trophy in sport, as in the FA Cup

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word also is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Something on top of a sports trophy, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ALSO to OLAS; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Small domes crown roofs, so they are architectural features that top buildings.

clue.text: Really there's no point in meeting

indicators.note: there's no says something has been taken away from the word Really

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone protests that there really is no point in having a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the compass point E from REALLY leaves the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass gathering of supporters is a political meeting.

clue.text: I'm nude, see? Horrible ! Old ladies furious !

indicators.note: horrible says the letters are turned into something ugly, a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A shocked elderly woman is outraged by someone undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Furies, avenging goddesses, were euphemistically called 'the kindly ones'; 'Horrible' rearranges IMNUDESEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies of Greek myth were ancient female avenging spirits, so the old ladies are mythically furious.

clue.text: Wound up insane

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to wound with a knife is to stab

explanation.surface: Someone has become so tense they have gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' reads as tense; it is STAB written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad, from having bats in the belfry, so crazy.

clue.text: Light, lively chap holds return of service

indicators.note: holds says one part is clasped inside the other

parts.note: a goer is an energetic, lively person

indicators.note: return of signals the word for service is read backwards

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A nimble player at tennis gets the ball back after a serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of service' suggests tennis; it is SSAM, MASS turned round, inside GOER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine cobweb threads are a byword for something delicate and weightless, so light.

clue.text: From choice of two I omitted anaesthetic

indicators.note: omitted says the following letter is left out

parts.note: either is the word for one or the other of two

explanation.surface: A patient picks between two options and skips the anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is a link; removing I from EITHER leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A volatile liquid once widely inhaled to put surgical patients to sleep, an early anaesthetic.

clue.text: Cut design to modify giant oil-rise

indicators.note: to modify something is to change it, so the letters are changed round

explanation.surface: Engineers alter a huge oil installation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to modify' rearranges GIANT OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraved or incised figure cut into stone or gem, a sunken carved design.

clue.text: A set-back in parliament's work programme ?

definitions.meaning: an alcove or niche set back into a wall
a break in the sitting of parliament, a gap in its programme

explanation.surface: A setback for the government's legislative timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' reads as a reverse but is a niche set back in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove in a wall and a holiday from parliamentary sittings share the one name.

clue.text: Versatile scholars in technical school science

parts.note: a poly is the short form of polytechnic, a British college of technical education
mathematics, maths in British usage, is a science

explanation.surface: Learned all-rounders are found studying science at a technical college.
explanation.walkthrough: A POLY was a British polytechnic, a college for technical and vocational study; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: People of wide learning across many fields are versatile scholars, the classic Renaissance all-rounders.

clue.text: "——, vain deluding joys" (Milton)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing first word of the opening line of Milton's poem Il Penseroso

explanation.surface: A line of Milton with its first word blanked out for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: Il Penseroso opens by banishing frivolous pleasures; the missing word is an archaic command meaning 'go away from here'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Milton's line the word is an imperative of dismissal, meaning 'away from here', the old sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Betting did not arise in Goodwood initially

parts.note: to lay in, like a lie-in, is to stay in bed and not get up

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the word Goodwood

explanation.surface: Someone at Goodwood races stayed in bed rather than go and bet.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodwood is an English racecourse in Sussex, which suits the betting surface; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers lay odds, offering a wager against a horse, so laying is the act of betting.

clue.text: Miss Bell's change of name would lack style

definitions.text: Miss Bell's change of name would lack style

parts.words: Miss Bell's change of name would lack style
parts.note: after a wedding Miss Bell takes her husband's surname and also loses the style of address Miss

explanation.surface: A remark that Miss Bell's new name would be inelegant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style' looks like elegance, but it is the formal style of address: the event that renames Miss Bell also strips her of the title Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedlock is the event that traditionally changes a woman's surname and her title from Miss to Mrs.

clue.text: Dives like a whale in the straits

definitions.meaning: a whale plunges deep, the verb used of whales diving
narrow sea channels, as in Puget or Plymouth channels of water, are called by this name

explanation.surface: A whale plunging down through a narrow sea passage.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means a whale diving steeply; the noun means narrow channels of sea, so both senses share one spelling.

clue.text: Part of joint attempt to win price war

definitions.meaning: the tender cut beneath the ribs in a sirloin of beef
to charge less than a rival to win business

explanation.surface: Joint efforts in a pricing battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's name for the tenderloin under the sirloin, and a verb for selling more cheaply than competitors.

clue.text: State guards against entry of soft goods

parts.note: Tex is an abbreviation for Texas, a US state
roof tiles keep the rain from getting in, so they guard against its entry

explanation.surface: A state government protects home industry by restricting imports of fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards against entry' reads as border protection but it is roof covering keeping weather out.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft goods is a trade term for cloth and fabric products, the woven materials of the drapery trade.

clue.text: H. Percy Jnr's dropped from its team

definitions.text: H. Percy Jnr's dropped from its team

indicators.note: dropped from says one name is taken out of the longer one

parts.note: the football club named after the London district is Tottenham Hotspur
Sir Henry Percy the younger, of Shakespeare's Henry IV, was nicknamed Hotspur

explanation.surface: A young player called Percy has been left out of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club named after Harry Hotspur; drop Hotspur and the district's name remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The north London district gave its name to the football club that also bears Hotspur's name.

clue.text: Ends sadly without mince pies to hand out

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, wrapping round another piece
sadly suggests something badly done, so the letters are reordered
to mince is to chop up, so these letters are cut and mixed

explanation.surface: A sad end for someone with no mince pies to give away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' turns ENDS into DNSE, and 'without' (outside) puts it around ISPE, from 'mince' acting on PIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute or deal out goods is to give them out, hand them out.

clue.text: It is cad's perversion to be so cruel

indicators.note: a perversion is a twisting out of its proper form, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Being so cruel is the twisted character of a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perversion' rearranges ITISCADS; the possessive 's of cad's counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes pleasure in inflicting pain is cruel in that specific deliberate way.

clue.text: Hardly a mark on the church …

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on skin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Barely a blemish on the church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' is the old adverbial sense, as in 'scarce believable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb the word means barely or only just, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Heard cruise timekeeper getting hit

definitions.meaning: cruise said aloud is crews, and the oarsman nearest the stern sets the rowing rate, the crew's timekeeper
a blow, as in a ... of the axe

explanation.surface: Someone on a cruise heard the ship's clock and was struck.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is itself a pun: 'Heard cruise' says crews, and in a rowing eight this oarsman keeps the timing for the whole crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The rower setting the pace for a crew and a single blow share this name; 'getting' is a link.

clue.text: … where Diana was worshipped

parts.note: the Roman goddess Diana is the Greek Artemis, whose great temple stood in an ancient Ionian city

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: the church where a goddess was revered.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie it to 18 down's 'church': this city had both the Temple of Artemis (Diana) and an early Christian church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionian city near modern Selçuk housed the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders.

clue.text: Flying boats ?

parts.note: flying boats are seaplanes, but read as vessels that fly the words describe lighter-than-air craft

explanation.surface: A seaplane that lands on water.
explanation.walkthrough: Flying boats are seaplanes; but a vessel that sails through the air rather than the sea is a balloon craft called a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirigibles were built and crewed like vessels of the sky, so they are aerial vessels that fly.

clue.text: Philosopher accepting a pound from this poet

parts.note: David Hume was the Scottish philosopher
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A thinker takes payment from a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Hulme was an English Imagist poet; 'from this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: T. E. Hulme was an Edwardian writer of verse, an Imagist poet and critic.

clue.text: Uneatable toast

parts.note: toast here is not grilled bread but a drink to someone's wellbeing, which cannot be eaten

explanation.surface: Burnt bread that nobody can eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' suggests bread; the toast meant is the raised glass, as in 'your good ...!' or 'drink a ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinkers raise glasses to someone's wellbeing; to drink a person's wellbeing is a toast that cannot be eaten.

clue.text: Split tenancy is feasible

parts.note: a let is a rental, a tenancy
on means possible, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A divided flat-share is workable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' is slang for tell or reveal a secret, not divided; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal a secret, informal for telling or splitting on someone.

clue.text: Horseplay in which Italian artist loses cravat

indicators.note: loses means a piece is taken away

parts.note: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was a Venetian painter
a cravat is a tie

explanation.surface: An Italian painter loses his neckwear in some rough fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horseplay' looks like rough fooling, but here is a game played on horseback; 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A team ball game played on horseback, quite literally play on horses.

clue.text: Old rustic about to play Irish hockey

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
hurling is the Irish stick game like hockey, so to hurl is to play it

explanation.surface: An old countryman is just about to join a game of Irish hockey.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurling is Ireland's fast stick-and-ball field game; 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaically a peasant or countryman was called this, before it came to mean a boorish person.

clue.text: Novices spoiled pets with honey,

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined or messed up, so the letters given are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beginner owners pamper their pets by feeding them honey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges PETS and HONEY; 'with' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or recent convert to any field or church is a beginner, so novices.

clue.text: Emerging situations giving negative results?

parts.note: unfolding events, but read in photography, processing film is what yields negatives

explanation.surface: New circumstances that turn out badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negative results' looks like bad outcomes, but in photography developing film produces negatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfolding events are new turns of the situation, and in darkroom work processing film yields negatives.
